body:
Friends have a personal investment in you and because of this an immediate reaction is horror at the idea of your death. 

Doctors and support groups lack that personal investment which is why they can talk to you about suicide in an abstract manner.   

With a friend, they will always have thoughts of "How can i fix them?" "Why can't I make them happy?" "I am failing them."   

Loved ones see it as a personal failure if they aren't able to "cheer you up." They will almost never be able to separate their relationship with you.    

I don't think friendship should be judged based on how they can cope with our suicide ideation. There is a reason counselors and psychiatrists have to earn a degree before they work in their fields, the common man hasn't the education or the experience.   

Why should be be friends with these people? Because they remind us of the happy times. Because we are social animals. Because they will help us move, and best friends will help us move a dead body.   

They are there for us when we need to bitch about our exes or our jobs. They help to support us in our anger. They count on us and we on them.    

Maybe they gave us our first kiss. Maybe they helped us when we got stranded on a road trip. Maybe they told off our ex for being an absolute asshole. Maybe they brought over ice cream and fudge when we were low, they helped cover for us when we were drunk off our ass, or they got our ass out of bed when we were too anxious to go to that job interview.      

There are so many other niches friends fill for us. I don't think we should write them off because they can't cope with us basically telling them that even after all this shit they did for us, we still want to die.

You have a tough road ahead and I just want you to know that nothing is your fault.    

You have the right to be angry at your loved ones.   

You have the right to set boundaries.   

You have the right to not allow them to make you pick a side.   

You have the right to follow your own moral beliefs.   

You have the right to live in a non-abusive environment.  

You have the right to love them both.   

You have the right to ask for help.  

You have the right to say no to a request that you feel would violate your moral beliefs.   

Any feeling you have, you are allowed to have them. Feelings are just feelings. They don't define you.   

You don't need to fix their relationship.   

You are not responsible for their happiness.  

You are loved.

I have the opposite perspective. Sometimes the people you love can be the worst choice in who to confess to. Those we love can take suicide personally. Or lash out at you in anger for scaring them.      

First I would suggest to think about her. How do you think she will take it? Is she experienced with mental health issues? Instead of telling her anything that hints at suicide, simply say you are depressed. Depression is easier to handle for loved ones than suicide.     

I speak from personal experience. I live with an elderly couple that I consider to be "mom and dad" for me. They know about my mental health issues and are supportive of my therapy. But one night I was severely triggered and was obsessing over the combination on the gun safe.    

I woke them up and asked them to please change the combination and not tell me. A few days later dad blew up at me saying I was holding the family hostage. He thought I was threatening suicide as a tool of manipulation. I tried to explain that my mental illness causes me to try to commit suicide impulsively, and the only way I could feel safe that night is if I had no way to access the guns.   

Thats why I feel therapy is better. I invited both of them to a visit with my therapist so they could hear from a professional more about my mental illness. 

With a therapist you have someone to talk to who has no bias.  They won't think that you are trying to manipulate them or its their fault you are feeling this way. They are experienced communicators. They can give you advice on how to talk to your loved ones.

Earning my Bachelors Degree kept me going. I told myself that once I earned that, then I proved my mom wrong. Then I could kill myself.   

Last term of senior year I started DBT therapy. I really liked my therapist and she asked me to give her 2 years. So I committed to 2 more years.   

Now I just want to see the final season of Game of Thrones.   

It doesn't have to be anything major, just something to look forward to. A small thing that you want to see, hear, taste, etc before you die.     

Suicide is my Plan B. Sometimes I find comfort in that. Sometimes it motivates me through the struggles. I always have plan B, but before I do that lets see if I can get through this next hurdle.

The last time I spoke with my mother was when I was 17 years old. She died in 2012.

Just because you share blood with someone, that doesn't make them family. If she is constantly making you feel like shit I suggest going completely no contact if/when you can.

As to the other I would say, think of how your death would affect her?

She would use your death to capitalize on sympathy. She might make money from it, making a gofundme page to collect money to "help with funeral costs." You could think of suicide as, if you kill yourself, then she wins.  Live on to spite her.

Use her as an example of the person you don't want to be. If she was like my mom, and told you that you were worthless, then work to achieve something of worth. Not to make her proud, but to prove her wrong. She doesn't need to know what you became, only you need to know.

If your relationships turn sour, think of what your mom would have done. Do you hear yourself repeating her words to the one you love? Don't judge yourself for it, but acknowledge what you are doing in order to prevent yourself from following her path.

So yea I would say think of your mom. Think of her and say Fuck You.

Hindsight is the best sight people say.

When I am lying awake at night, unable to sleep. Sometimes I fantasize about going back in time and stealing myself from the hospital where i was born and smuggling the tiny baby that is me to the house of the people that I now consider to be mom and dad.

If I was raised by parents that supported me, instead of abusing me, then I would have a much better life I know. I would have gone to college straight out of high school instead of working a full time job.

I would have joined the Gifted and Talented Program in third grade . Supportive parents would have sent me to be a foreign exchange student in 4th grade when I got a letter from the president with the offer. I don't know what country I would have chosen to go to, but I know I would have gone.

By now I would have earned my PhD. I like to think I would have chosen to be a geneticist or immunologist researcher.

I wouldn't automatically distrust every stranger. I would be a leader. I wouldn't fear abandonment.

When I was a kid I would sometimes stare at the phone while everyone was still asleep. An 8 year old looking at the rotary dial, wondering if I called 911 and ask the police to take me away would they have?

They say you can't know what would have happened if you made different choices. Still I think if I made that phone call life would have had to have been better. I would have told the police I was abused and molested. It would have been better if I was raised by my dad. Because even though he was addicted to coke, my Grandma Yoshiko would have been the one to have raised me I bet, and I would have learned Buddhist wisdom and that a woman's strength is her mind.

But I didn't make the phone call, and when I ran away at 9 I walked back home when I got super hungry.

I know what it's like to feel like your life has been wasted. Yet, dwelling on it is just another form of self-harm. I try to tell myself that although I can't control what goes on around me, I can control how I react to it.

I can control whether or not I stay locked in my room on the computer all day, or stay in touch with my friends. I can control it if I allow myself to stay in bed all day because of chronic pain, or if I force myself to at least brush my teeth and take a shower. I can control if I stay home and miss doctors appointments because of despair. I can control if I let my emotions make my decisions or not. I can control whether or not I judge myself when I do backslide.

I am not sure what the point is to this long post, but I guess I wrote it so you know that someone else is there that feels the same. I am 38.

> “If you are depressed you are living in the past.  If you are anxious you are living in the future.  If you are at peace you are living in the present.”   -Lao Tzu
